articleTitle: Exploring the Transformative Potential of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Mechanical Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The sophistication of technology has shown to offer several benefits in various fields. The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the potential to significantly improve any area of its integration, including Mechanical Engineering Education (MEE). A subset of AI, Generative Artificial Intelligence GAI) promises an invaluable potential in MEE. However, the promising potential of this technology hasn't been explored yet in the MEE context. Thus, this paper examines the publications that have been investigating the applications of AI in MEE to provide an overview of the possibility and the most suitable way of implementing GAI in MEE. Accordingly, this paper will provide future researchers a better understanding of how GAI can be integrated into MEE to aid Mechanical engineering (ME) students and faculty in utilizing these technologies and assist institutes in implementing these technologies in the ME curriculum.

articleTitle: Time Study Based Model to Optimize the Assembly Line Efficiency and Labor Cost Incorporating Human Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Human factors play an important role in the optimization of industrial processes. Factors such as a worker's skill, effort, condition, and consistency have a significant impact on his performance. The objective of this paper is to determine the effect of human factors on the efficiency of assembly lines and labor costs by using the Classical Westinghouse Method (CWM). Using a time study-based mathematical model, the efficiency of the assembly lines and labor costs are optimized by considering human factors such as workers' skill, effort, condition, and consistency. The model is validated by a time study of the serial manufacturing industry in Pakistan. In a nutshell, this model may enable the serial assembly line manufacturing industries to improve efficiency and optimize labor costs by taking human factors into account.

articleTitle: From Knowledge Management to a Learning Organization: Strategic Use of AI Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: With the proliferation of easily available AI tools in the market since the release of ChatGPT, there is evidence of their prompt adoption. While the short-term benefits to productivity are clear, we argue that for organizations to truly benefit from AI tool use, their interactions should be built upon the foundation of an organizational knowledge management strategy. When AI tools are connected to internal knowledge bases, they may reduce potential for hallucinations and mitigate loss of confidential, proprietary information. AI tools may contribute to all knowledge management activities, including knowledge storage and retrieval, knowledge creation, application and transfer. Upon successful integration, new internal knowledge may then be combined with external information to further organizational learning. To promote successful outcomes, we put forth several requirements, such as but not limited to appropriate, meaningful collaboration, joint task performance, and an organizational culture of continuous learning and change.

articleTitle: Combining Blockchain, IoT and AI for Food Safety Assurance: A Systemic Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Various issues are inherent in the traditional food supply chains that affect the quality and safety of the food items. These include contamination of food, fraudulent activities, inefficiencies, and lack of transparency. This research presents an integrated system to improve food safety management. The system implements blockchain to save the data safely, IoT to streamline real-time monitoring, and AI for predictive analysis. While previous research considered these individual components, the novelty of this study is its successful assembly into a single framework. The system reduces latency and improves decision-making across the supply chain by leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and edge computing. When the system underwent a pilot study, it was able to demonstrate its potential for improving operational efficiency and reducing waste. The reaction time to food safety incidents decreased by 30%, and spoilage detection accuracy increased from 10-15% to 25%. In addition, this research demonstrates a theoretical framework for technology integration in supply chains and provides feasible methods to improve the food security level through the application of technologies and quality assurance. It created a performance benchmark for technological applications regarding food safety.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Predictive Analytics in Workload Distribution for Forensic Engineering Case Reporting Process: Dubai Police Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The Dubai Police Forensic Engineering Department plays a significant role in forensic investigations, where efficient case reporting is essential for effective case resolution and the overall success of investigative outcomes. However, the department faces significant challenges in the workload distribution among examiners and reviewers, which directly leads to extended lead times and delays in case reporting. Therefore, this paper aims to address the challenge of unbalanced workload distribution of cases and its impact on case reporting by proposing a machine learning-driven solution, utilizing predictive analytics to facilitate case reporting, reduce lead times, and enhance the efficiency of forensic engineering operations based on the findings of an earlier study that identified significant inefficiencies within case reporting. By using historical case data, this paper applied predictive algorithms to identify patterns in case categories, incident types, and examiner allocation. Concept Explorer was used to generate variable combinations, while MATLAB was used to develop the predictive model that predicts the working days of different combinations. The findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning-driven solutions in achieving the department's goal of reducing average case reporting times to 7 days. The model reduced the working days for selected cases from an initial range of 1 ≤ WD ≤ 17 to a range of 6 ≤ WD ≤ 10, resulting in more balanced workloads and shorter lead times.

articleTitle: Design of a Sustainable Multimodal Transportation Network for Waste Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This research aims to support informed decision-making by quantifying the impact of multimodal transportation on the eco-efficiency of waste transportation networks, focusing on various transportation strategies. This study integrates maritime and road transport within the waste management system to enhance operational efficiency and reduce costs. A mathematical modeling approach, specifically a linear programming model, is employed to optimize waste transportation from collection points to recycling facilities. Using real-world data from a case study in Quebec province (Canada), our numerical analysis shows that a multimodal approach (road and maritime) can reduce transportation costs by 14% and greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) by 27%. Incorporating external transportation costs leads to a 31% decrease in greenhouse gas emissions and a 13% reduction in expenses compared to the current scenario.

articleTitle: Technologies in Construction Industry: A Study on the Challenges of Innovative Technologies Adoption in the GCC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The construction industry is increasingly adopting innovative technologies to enhance project delivery, improve efficiency, and facilitate collaboration among stakeholders. However, the successful integration of these technologies is significantly hindered by a range of interdependent challenges, including regulatory hurdles, economic constraints, organizational resistance, management issues, and technical limitations. This study aims to explore these challenges through semi-structured interviews with four subject matter experts in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) sector. Their insights shed light on the complexities of technology adoption, revealing not only established barriers but also emerging obstacles that have yet to be thoroughly investigated in existing literature. By identifying both recognized and novel challenges, this research seeks to provide a comprehensive understanding of the difficulties faced during the adoption of innovative technologies in construction. Furthermore, the study will propose targeted strategies to overcome these challenges, offering actionable recommendations tailored for organizations in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region. These findings aim to guide stakeholders in navigating the intricate landscape of technology adoption, ultimately fostering a more efficient and innovative construction environment.

articleTitle: Integrating Bibliometrics with Design Thinking to Enhance Technological Innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The integration of bibliometrics into an innovation process such as design thinking has the potential to enhance innovation engineering management by providing a comprehensive understanding and valuable insights of the research landscape in a particular domain to support divergent problem and solution phases. This research paper examines and demonstrates the potential benefits and practicability of methodically and operatively incorporating bibliometric scanning into the design thinking process. Thereby, an adapted approach consisting of bibliometric problem and solution scanning is presented and applied to the fields of fuel tank maintenance and robot locomotion in confined spaces. The approach generated a general overview of scientific production based on total publications as well as average citations and identified key concepts and collaborations in the respective fields through cooccurrence and co-authorship network analyses. Two hypotheses regarding the content-related advances respectively the applicability from the innovation team perspective were developed and tested. The results supported both hypotheses and revealed that bibliometrics can complement and enhance the design thinking process by providing data driven knowledge to divergent problem understanding and solution ideation phases. By leveraging the insights obtained from bibliometric scanning, innovation teams can efficiently build on existing knowledge, uncover new opportunities and make more informed and comprehensible decisions to ultimately create more impactful solutions.

articleTitle: An Exploration of Smart Tourism Ecosystem from the Value Co-Creation Lens A Case Study in China
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: With the development of smart tourism, more cities are starting to make investment and construction regarding smart tourism. Yet despite the advanced technologies that cities are adopting, the tourist experience remains paramount. Therefore, this paper adopts the perspective of value co-creation theory to study the smart tourism ecosystem to emphasise innovation service and tourist experience for the sustainable development of the industry. This paper derives a framework for smart tourism ecosystems through a case study in Yunnan Province, China. It also explores in depth how different players, namely tourists, government and service providers, can engage in value co-creation in commanding the tourism ecosystem. Finally, the paper proposes a model that can be applied to the platform ecosystem that includes value proposition, value-in-exchange, and value-in-use with smart tourism actors.

articleTitle: Integrating Blockchain, Industry 4.0 and Emerging Technologies in the Logistics of Circular Economy: Theoretical Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: A systematic literature review was conducted using the Scopus database to analyze logistics in the circular economy, focusing on areas such as blockchain, industry 4.0, and emerging technologies based on 116 research publications. It provides a detailed review of the impact of the circular economy on logistical operations and sustainability, through content and bibliographic analysis. The research identifies important trends, gaps, and key success factors across environmental, economic, social, security, and administrative domains. These factors will help create a framework for testing technology applications in circular economy logistics in organizations like GE HealthCare, Hologic, Philips, and Siemens, offering valuable insights for both academia and industry.

articleTitle: Digital Lean Practices in High-Mix, Low-Volume Manufacturing: A Case Study of Manitowoc
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The transition from mass production to increased customization exposes companies to challenges, particularly in the low-volume, high-mix sector. In this regard, Lean practices and digitalization were applied in this research work at Manitowoc - a global leader in crane manufacturing - to improve production process performance characteristics. Consequently, digitizing work standards and visual management helped the company to minimize errors and enhance operational quality. These have led to tremendous decrease of color mistakes as well as improve resource optimization that strengthened self-control and accountability of teams over their tasks.

articleTitle: Towards a Behaviour Model for Drones Integration in Agile Manufacturing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), commonly known as drones, have emerged as a promising technology with significant potential in various industries. This paper addresses the integration of UAVs within the context of Intralogistics 4.0, focusing on their practical applications in manufacturing environments. The study aims to bridge the existing gap between the technological capabilities of drones and their effective utilization in industrial settings by providing a MILP formulation to evaluate its feasibility.

articleTitle: Rotary Machines Fault Detection and Diagnosis Using Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: FaultDetection and Diagnosis (FDD) of rotary components is a critical issue. This paper aims to address critical challenges in maintaining rotating machinery, such as pumps and motors, with a specific focus on minimizing downtime, reducing operational costs, and enhancing equipment reliability. The work highlights common issues, including false alarms, faulty signals, and difficulties distinguishing between normal and abnormal operational conditions, all of which impact the effectiveness of maintenance strategies. The methodology involves training machine learning (ML) models, including Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), on actual historical data collected from SCADA systems. One of the largest pumping stations of the Dubai Municipality was selected for the implementation of ML methods. Data was obtained for this station, addressing thirteen inputs across 92 instances (with 74 signals classified as normal and 18 as abnormal). Subsequently, several ML models were tested on the data, and their performance was validated through field troubleshooting. The evaluation focuses on determining the “best” model in terms of fault detection accuracy, precision, recall, and other performance metrics. The findings offer valuable insights for optimizing predictive maintenance (PdM) strategies, reducing unscheduled downtime, and improving operational efficiency in pump stations. This research contributes to the field by providing a comprehensive approach to integrating advanced ML techniques with FDD, delivering actionable insights for the Dubai Municipality and similar industrial applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Weather on Radio-Frequency Energy Harvesting Efficiency: Review and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: With the rise of IoT and smart cities, there is a need for reliable and eco-friendly power. Radio Frequency Energy Harvesting (RF-EH) is an example of a low environmental footprint and wide availability that can power Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) in urban environments. Although RF-EH has many advantages, its operational efficiency under various weather conditions such as temperature, humidity, and wind remains understudied. This paper summarizes the existing literature on RF-EH and highlights some discrepancies in the way these environmental factors affect system performance. We propose the development of an adaptive algorithm that adapts to changing weather conditions. This would increase the resilience and functionality of RF-EH for smart city infrastructures.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Sustainable Microprocessor Utilization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper examines the integration of machine learning advancements with microprocessor hardware to enhance speed and energy efficiency. It reviews recent studies and promising approaches addressing existing challenges. Beyond this primary focus, the paper explores related technologies such as quantum computing, neuromorphic computing, and 3D stacking, as well as emerging fields like photonic computing, highlighting their potential synergies with machine learning to further improve microprocessor performance.

articleTitle: Predicting Automobile Insurance Claim Rate Versus Through Severity and Frequency Predictions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: We consider a Regression problem in which the Target is a function of two or more variables. One can either predict the target value directly or predict the component variables and then compute the Target value. A common example is automobile insurance claims. One can compute Frequency and Severity separately and then take the product to determine the amount claimed per year (which we call the Total Claim Severity or Claim Rate) or one may compute the claims paid per year for each customer and then predict this value directly. We show that theoretically, the performance is better if one predicts the computed value (e.g., Total Claim Severity) directly rather than predicting the individual components (e.g., frequency and severity) and then calculating the Total Claim Severity as the product. We illustrate the differences experimentally using data for customers from a real insurance company.

articleTitle: Impact of Digital Transformation on Conventional Business Models: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The digital transformation of the business strategy powered by the adoption of advanced technology in various organisations has profusely improved performance, productivity, and efficiency globally. The strategic adoption and integration of these new technologies in the traditional business models have been helpful in the scalability of various companies' operations. This literature review explores several research papers with specific keywords related to digital transformation within traditional business models. The study, through literature reviews, aims to investigate the impact of digital transformation on the conventional business model of organisations, with the primary context considering several multinational companies. The methodology sorted various literature sources using some keywords to explore and evaluate the impact, factors, challenges, theories, and strategic adoption of digital technologies and transformations in business models. The sorted and used research works are carefully selected not to be more than five years old to ensure that recent technologies are captured. The study identifies the factors, challenges and strategies that could impact the strategic integration of advanced technology in traditional business models within various organisations to explore their full benefits and potential. The impact of these was explored and noticed in customer satisfaction, budget and funding, and constraints of modern technology adoption due to change management. The critical analysis of this study identifies a conceptual framework and research gaps that could be addressed in future research.

articleTitle: Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning for Selective Maintenance with Learning Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for addressing selective maintenance problems with imperfect repairs over a finite horizon. The proposed approach relies on two deep Q-learning architectures to optimize system reliability while minimizing maintenance costs, incorporating both learning effects on maintenance durations and energy consumption optimization. To further enhance the proposed framework, we integrate case-based reasoning, allowing the system to draw insights from previously solved cases. Applied to a real-world coal transportation system, the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms, delivering high-quality solutions with minimal computational effort. The results support the significant role of case-based reasoning and learning effects in improving overall system performances.

articleTitle: Robots Path Planning in RoboCup Competitions: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper explores and evaluates various path planning approaches in RoboCup competitions, aiming to advance AI research and address real-world challenges. The criteria for evaluation include computational efficiency, path optimality, adaptability to dynamic environments, and real-time performance. The study highlights the importance of path planning for autonomous navigation in dynamic environments, emphasizing the need for efficient and optimal travel routes. It reviews methodologies across different RoboCup leagues, noting a research focus on the Small Size League (SSL) and a gap in studies for other leagues like Rescue, Logistics, and Humanoid. Key findings include the effectiveness of heuristic approaches like A* algorithms, the potential of metaheuristics such as genetic algorithms, and the promise of machine learning (ML) methods. The paper suggests future research directions, including the development of hybrid approaches, enhanced ML techniques, and real-time responsive algorithms. The integration of multiple strategies and exploration of under-researched leagues could significantly advance robotic path planning.

articleTitle: Perception of the Use of Recycled Construction Waste in the UAE's Construction Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The UAE's construction industry faces significant challenges due to increasing volumes of construction and demolition waste (CDW). This study examines factors affecting stakeholders' perceptions of using recycled CDW materials, with an emphasis on Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) to validate key perception dimensions. Six critical dimensions were evaluated: Awareness and Knowledge, Benefits, Barriers, External Influences, Organizational Resources and Support, and Effectiveness. The analysis reveals that barriers related to quality, aesthetic, and regulatory concerns hinder positive perceptions, while external influences and benefits significantly support CDW acceptance. Insights suggest that policy interventions, improved material standards, and investment in recycling infrastructure are pivotal to advancing sustainable construction in the UAE.

articleTitle: Assessment of Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) Models in the Healthcare Commodities Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper evaluates Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) models in the healthcare commodity industry, focusing on five models: Vendor Replenished Inventory (VRI), Vendor Managed Inventory Services (VMIS), Third Party Replenished Inventory (3RI), Third Party Managed Inventory Services (3MIS), and Inventory Management Technical Assistance (IMTA). Each model is assessed based on five criteria: inventory management scope, flexibility vs. benefit, the role of the VMI partner, visibility, and responsibility. The study highlights the advantages of VMI, such as reduced bullwhip effect and improved coordination, while also addressing challenges like outdated data exchange and inaccurate demand forecasting. The findings indicate that VMSI ranks highest across all criteria, followed by 3MIS and 3RI, which perform well but face visibility and responsibility challenges. VRI shows good performance but lacks the supplementary services of VMIS. IMTA, while flexible, ranks lower due to its complexities in transitioning responsibilities. This evaluation aims to guide healthcare supply chain managers in selecting the most appropriate VMI model to enhance supply chain efficiency and ensure the reliable provision of essential healthcare commodities.

articleTitle: Enhancing PII Detection in Student Essays: A Longformer-Based Approach with Synthetic Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper investigates the efficacy of Microsoft's Presidio SDK for detecting Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in student essays. It evaluates the performance of a fine-tuned Longformer model as an alternative. While Presidio is widely adopted for PII recognition across domains, we explore its effectiveness within a novel domain-specific dataset comprising 22,000 student essays from a Vanderbilt University MOOC. The dataset's PII annotations include categories such as student names, email addresses, and phone numbers. Our study hypothesizes that a customized Longformer model, fine-tuned on a domain-specific, human-annotated dataset, will significantly outperform Presidio in PII detection, particularly for context-sensitive entities. To address label imbalance in the training data, we augment it with 1,000 synthetically generated essays. The Longformer model's architecture combines local and global attention mechanisms, enabling effective processing of long-form text. Our results demonstrate that the Longformer model trained with synthetic data augmentation achieves superior performance, with an F5 score of 0.936, compared to Presidio's 0.735. These findings underscore the importance of domain-specific datasets and synthetic data augmentation for enhancing PII detection in specialized text corpora.

articleTitle: Leveraging Industry 4.0 Technologies for Reverse Logistics Financial Performance: a Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Despite the growing interest in Industry 4.0 (I4.0) technologies, their implementations across various fields, and their potential role in improving reverse logistics (RL) operations; the financial advantages of I4.0 technologies remain unexplored and lacking in application. This study deployed a systematic literature review (SLR) to identify and examine the key I4.0 technologies applicable in RL operations, and their implications on financial outcomes, to propose a novel taxonomy of reverse logistics financial performance (RLFP), and to suggest directions for further investigations. A state-of-the-art SLR of relevant peer-reviewed RLFP published between 2000 and 2023 is conducted. The qualified studies are evaluated qualitatively using template analysis through dynamic capability theory (DCT). Results indicated that I4.0 technologies positively influence RLFP, with artificial intelligence (AI), big data, advanced robotics, and internet-of-things (IoT) demonstrating dominant effects on financial results. However, findings revealed limited research efforts on cyber-physical systems (CPS), cloud computing, and cognitive computing as I4.0 technologies, indicating a substantial gap in the literature. Results suggested that operational efficiency, flexibility, risk management, and real-time visibility are the key financial performance metrics for I4.0 technology adoption. Findings further emphasized that the application of I4.0 improves competitive advantage, revenue generation opportunities, customer satisfaction, and cash flow improvement, and lowers operational expenses, which drives RLFP.

articleTitle: Identification of Suitable Maintenance Strategy for Medical Devices in UAE Healthcare Facilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: In the healthcare system, advanced medical devices such as ventilators, defibrillators, and dialysis machines are essential. Effective maintenance strategies are critical to ensure the continuous and safe operation of these devices. This study explores the use of the Quality Function Deployment (QFD) method to identify suitable maintenance strategies for ventilator devices in UAE intensive care units. A survey of healthcare professionals was conducted in the UAE, results identified nine key customer requirements, in which safety (5), and efficiency (4) prioritized higher than remaining attributes. These requirements were then mapped to technical maintenance solutions such as scheduled maintenance, spare parts management, emergency repair protocols, predictive analytics, and energy efficiency. The QFD results ranked spare parts management (138), and emergency repair protocols (96) as the first and second important technical requirements respectively. These requirements fall under preventive and corrective maintenance strategies. Therefore, the possible strategies should be implemented to ensure the efficiency and safety of ventilators in healthcare system. Prioritizing preventive maintenance protocols can enhance the operational efficiency and reliability of ventilator devices, which is crucial for patient safety in UAE healthcare facilities.

articleTitle: An IoT-Driven Framework for Blood Supply Chain Management: Addressing Demand-Supply Uncertainties in the UAE Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper introduces an IoT-driven framework specifically designed for Blood Supply Chain Management (BSCM) in the UAE, beginning with a comprehensive analysis of the current state of the blood supply chain. The analysis reveals significant issues, such as substantial wastage of blood units and non-uniform demand across hospitals, with instances where wastage surpasses actual demand. To address these challenges, the proposed framework integrates advanced technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, artificial intelligence (AI), and big data analytics to create a highly responsive and efficient blood supply network. By leveraging real-time data capture and analysis, the system ensures optimal alignment of blood product availability with hospital and clinic needs, thereby reducing wastage and improving healthcare outcomes. It discusses the implementation of this framework in the UAE, examining how such technological innovations can mitigate common challenges in BSCM such as perishability, variable demand, and logistical constraints. The study aims to provide a robust solution that enhances the effectiveness of the Blood Supply Chain (BSC), ultimately leading to better patient care and resource management in the healthcare system. Through detailed case studies and empirical analysis, this paper illustrates the potential for IoT technologies to transform BSC operations by enhancing transparency, efficiency, and reliability in managing blood resources in the UAE.

articleTitle: A Case Study of Social Media Analytics for Effective Digital Marketing in Textile Circularity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Today, as most organizations navigate through digital transformation, the pressing concerns of environmental issues elevate sustainability and the circular economy to critical positions on corporate agendas. To address this gap, this study adopts a case study over Instagram© to combine descriptive and content analyses to extract insightful data. The results reveal that distinct contrasts are evident between passive viewing and active participation on social media, highlighting a need for strategies that better foster meaningful engagement. The effectiveness of content in engaging users is crucial, particularly when it employs positive sentiments and specific formats, which tend to attract more interaction. Furthermore, the pivotal roles of key hashtags and influential social media users in linking various sustainability discussions are instrumental in shaping broader awareness and discourse. This paper contributes to the field by offering insights that can refine digital marketing strategies and improve stakeholder engagement in the textile industry, emphasizing the importance of nuanced customer behavior analysis.

articleTitle: A System Dynamics Approach for Assessing the Sustainability Impacts of Pink Fuels in Taxi Transportation in UAE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Fossil fuels such as coal, oil, and natural gas release greenhouse gases into the environment, leading to environmental, economic, social, and health concerns. A major obstacle stands in energy and transportation industries reducing their reliance on fossil fuels and their carbon footprint. To lessen these impacts, it is necessary to decrease or eradicate the carbon footprint, and alternative carbon-free energy sources must be pursued. Hydrogen has been suggested as a feasible energy source for the transportation sector to solve this problem without emitting greenhouse gases. This research investigates the sustainability impact of hydrogen fuel transportation (specifically taxis) in the UAE. It will employ “pink” hydrogen fuel that has not been discussed in previous research in transportation services to evaluate hydrogen fuel demand and to develop a hydrogen fuel system to lower carbon emissions and promote a low-carbon economy. A System Dynamics (SD) model is built to analyze factors influencing future demand for hydrogen fuel. This model will connect elements through qualitative causal loop diagrams, addressing barriers such as fuel prices, hydrogen adoption rates, economic and environmental impacts, infrastructure, policy and technological innovation, stakeholder behavior, and taxi fleet profiles. This will allow for evaluating the factors that endorse hydrogen's progress and classify barriers that delay it. The results of the causal-loop diagram integrated into the SD model will reveal the key factors driving the demand for Pink Hydrogen fuels in taxi transportation. It will also assess stakeholder contributions to determine the long-term sustainability impacts of hydrogen fuel adoption in the UAE.

articleTitle: Industry 4.0 Deciphered: Mapping Key Technologies Adoption in Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: In recent years, the world's industrial environment has changed dramatically due to continuous technological development and innovation in manufacturing processes. Manufacturers are incorporating new technologies into their production facilities and their operations to facilitate real-time decision-making, enhanced productivity, flexibility and agility. The idea to empower the manufacturing sector through digitization, Industry 4.0 (I4.0), emerged at the German Hannover Fair in 2011 and has received added attention in academic literature but does not yet have a clear definition. I4.0 is still in the early stages and continues to expand quickly. It has the potential to impact product design, manufacturing, delivery and payment processes. Despite its growing importance, I4.0 is still not widely understood and is not yet well-established in practice, making it challenging for businesses to adequately plan its adoption. Thus, a literature review is made to comprehend the I4.0 technologies and their adoption patterns across different industries. A conceptual framework is designed, based on a grouping criterion, to facilitate an indepth analysis of the relationship between the I4.0 technologies and their adoption in the supply chain. The paper also addresses the reasons why some technologies have a low adoption rate, identifies gaps in the literature reviewed, and suggests new avenues for future research.

articleTitle: Value-Driven Healthcare: Cost-Benefit ML Approach to AKI Management in Cardiac Surgery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) following cardiac surgery is a significant complication that impacts patient outcomes and healthcare costs. This study introduces a cost-sensitive predictive model integrating Random Forest (RF) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) algorithms to enhance the identification of AKI risk. Our model achieved a recall of 96%, demonstrating its high sensitivity in identifying at-risk patients, which is critical for minimizing missed diagnoses and improving early intervention strategies. By incorporating cost considerations into the machine learning framework, the model ensures a balance between clinical and economic outcomes, leading to an estimated net savings of $8,101,676 through optimized resource allocation and reduced complications. This work highlights the potential of integrating cost-sensitive methodologies with predictive modeling to promote value-driven healthcare and improve decision-making in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Optimizing Municipal Solid Waste Collection Using Smart Bins - A Case Study in United Arab Emirates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The inefficient static municipal solid waste collection (MSWC) routes pose challenges in urban waste management, resulting in high costs, fuel consumption, and emissions. Smart bins equipped with Internet-of-Things (IoT) technology enable real-time waste monitoring, reducing overflow and inefficiencies in waste management. In this study, further improvements are achieved by assuming the collection problem as a Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP) and optimizing the collection routes using a TSP solution algorithm and the Nearest Neighbor (NN) method. The objective of this paper is to determine the efficiency of implementing IoT in waste bins for MSWC routes for better waste collection. Integrating smart bins into MSWC enhances route optimization, yielding significant operational and environmental benefits. Through a simulation model developed in AnyLogic, the study demonstrates that integrating smart bins into MSWC routes can achieve significant reductions in travel distance and carbon emissions, underscoring the significant operational and environmental benefits of IoT-based waste management systems over traditional approaches. The novelty of this work lies in its innovative integration of Internet-of-Things (IoT) technology into municipal solid waste collection, utilizing a Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP) framework to optimize collection routes. This approach not only enhances real-time monitoring and efficiency but also significantly reduces operational costs and environmental impact, setting a new benchmark for smart waste management solutions.

articleTitle: Application of the Single-Order Model to Minimize Capital Costs and Project Delays: A Case Study for High-Value Inventories in Construction Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This paper presents an optimization model for managing costly inventories, specifically high-voltage transformers, in electrical construction projects, aimed at minimizing capital costs and project delays. The study applies the single-period inventory model, also known as the Newsvendor model, to determine the optimal order quantity at the project's start. Sensitivity analysis is performed on several parameters to assess the impact of each attribute on the optimal order quantity. The results show that lower success probabilities and higher under-ordering costs require larger order quantities to avoid shortages. Higher scrap values also increase the optimal orders, especially when unit costs are low. These findings highlight the importance of a flexible inventory strategy tailored to project-specific factors. The paper provides construction project managers with strategies to optimize inventory management, reducing costly delays and overruns. By applying the Newsvendor model, it supports better decision-making when ordering high-value components, such as high-voltage transformers, ensuring efficient project execution.

articleTitle: Assessing Blockchain-Based Platforms for Organic Food Supplychain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This research aims to find the best open-source blockchain platforms for use in agriculture, providing businesses with a solid foundation and helping them avoid the challenges of starting from scratch. The study began by reviewing 18 blockchain platforms and narrowing them down to 9 open-source options. It then used a combination of the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) to evaluate the platforms. Expert opinions and a thorough literature review focused on four key criteria: Transparency and Traceability, Security and Data Integrity, Cost Efficiency, and User Experience and Accessibility. The AHP analysis showed that Transparency and Traceability were the most important factors, while the TOPSIS evaluation highlighted Hyperledger Sawtooth as the top platform, excelling in all areas. The study underscores the importance of a multi-criteria decision-making approach in selecting blockchain solutions for agriculture, showing how open-source platforms can enhance efficiency, ensure data integrity, and build trust with consumers.

articleTitle: Adopting Sustainable Water-Waste Management Operations in the Mining Sector: An Integrated Research
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Considering the substantial environmental impact and consequences of resource conservation, sustainable water waste management in the mining industry is paramount. Transparency and practical methods for resolving water management issues are frequently lacking in current practices. To comply with legal requirements, lessen environmental impact, and encourage wise resource use, it is necessary to investigate and practice sustainable water waste management solutions. This study investigated sustainable water waste management practices in mining using a qualitative approach through case study methodology. A purposeful sampling technique was used to collect verifiable and varied case studies during the literature review and thematic analysis from various mining operations worldwide. The study's findings show the different degrees of environmental regulation compliance and the adoption of responsible practices with the execution of the proposed framework, revealing various water waste management solutions used by mining corporations. The selected case studies provide information on novel reporting initiatives and cutting-edge technologies that support more sustainable water management. The sector has made some strides towards more responsible water waste management, but there are still gaps in openness, data verification, and coordination. Overall, this study emphasizes the significance of sustainable water waste management in the mining industry and the requirement for proactive actions to overcome the associated difficulties. According to the study, attaining sustainable water waste management requires open reporting, regulatory compliance, and technology integration, as well as promoting ethical mining practices and encouraging the sector to use proposed frameworks that emphasize resource efficiency and environmental preservation.

articleTitle: Improving National Competitiveness Through the Optimized Allocation of Governmental Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: We investigate the impact of ICT adoption, skills of the workforce, and Research and Development (R&D) expenditure on a country's overall competitiveness score. This was done primarily with data from the World Economic Forum's 2019 Global Competitiveness Report but we also use several additional data sources. We used various regression models to analyse the relationships between these variables and competitiveness. The findings revealed that ICT adoption, skills of the workforce, and R&D expenditure all had a significant effect on improving overall competitiveness. The results also indicate that reducing mobile broadband service prices significantly improved ICT adoption, while fixed broadband service prices had a minimal impact on ICT adoption. In addition, education expenditure as a percentage of GDP was found to have minimal impact on improving workforce skills suggesting other factors might be more impactful. This research can provide an understanding of the key drivers of competitiveness and offer insights to policymakers. Given the impact of each factor on competitiveness, one can then allocate public resources to maximize the resulting impact on competitiveness. Such an analysis is presently underway.

articleTitle: Finlingo: A Conversational AI for Enhancing Financial Literacy Education in Africa
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Africa's Fintech revolution offers unprecedented financial opportunities, yet a persistent literacy gap hinders its full potential. Despite various educational initiatives, challenges in delivering effective financial education across diverse African contexts remain. This paper proposes the development of Finlingo, a conversational AI specifically designed to enhance digital financial literacy in Africa. Leveraging artificial intelligence, this tool aims to provide accurate, contextually relevant responses to a wide range of financial queries, addressing practical issues from basic concepts to complex financial products. By using natural language processing and machine learning, our approach seeks to overcome existing barriers, offering personalized, accessible, and up-to-date financial education. The AI system is designed to adapt to individual needs and encourage practical application of financial knowledge. This study contributes to ongoing efforts in promoting financial inclusion across Africa through an innovative, technology-driven solution, potentially bridging the gap between financial knowledge and effective decision-making.

articleTitle: Technological Disruption in Manufacturing - Redefining Buyer-Supplier Relationships and Business Models in the Industry 4.0 Era
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The impact of Industry 4.0-related technology shifts on buyer-supplier dynamics (BSD) is the subject of this research. As evidence, it draws on 17 expert interviews with manufacturing company managers in India. In order to infer meaning from the empirical data and discover overarching themes, patterns, and categories, a qualitative content analysis is carried out. The paper concludes that moving different value creation activities to platforms, digitised and automated procedures will form the basis of most future transactions in manufacturing supply chains. A more passionate character emerges in BSD. A company's supplier base may be streamlined by identifying and working with its most valuable strategic suppliers. Additional research may build on these findings by comparing and contrasting BSD across other sectors or stages of the value chain, and then drawing comparisons and highlighting commonalities. Management theory and business practise may both benefit from the findings presented in this article. As for BSD, they aid businesses in realising Industry 4.0's full promise by establishing and maintaining competitive advantages over the long run. Among the first to do so, this research uses Industry 4.0 to conduct an empirical investigation of BSD.

articleTitle: Modelling Churn as a Long-Term Profit Optimization Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: In typical recommender systems, the main goal would be to maximize the probability that customers would purchase the product/s that the system recommends. However, this method may be a double edged sword to some businesses as the products these recommender systems recommend to customers, while suitable for the customers, may not be very profitable for the company. Therein lies the delicate trade-off where the recommended products that are very profitable to a company may not be suitable for the customers which may cause them to switch to a competitor and vice versa. Therefore the products recommended must be both sufficiently suitable to the customer and sufficiently profitable to the company. This paper considers a recommender system with the goal of maximizing the long-term profit for a company (i.e., the sum of immediate profit made by the recommended product and the expected profit of future product purchases made by the customer). In this approach, the customer gains from obtaining favourable recommendations and the company benefits from acceptable profits from a long-term client. We compare long-term profits gained from a customer using the proposed approach with that of Recommender Systems that optimizes customer suitability as well as the company's immediate profit.

articleTitle: Sustainable ERP Systems: Current Trends, Challenges, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Sustainable Enterprise Resource Planning (S-ERP) systems are fundamental for embedding sustainability into organizational operations, enhancing environmental, social, and economic performance. However, deploying S-ERP systems is complex and presents many challenges, as evidenced by current studies. This review seeks to address the knowledge gap by examining the current state and implementation of S-ERP systems through an extensive literature review. The study identifies key factors for successful S-ERP adoption, including strategic planning, efficient data management, strong managerial support, multidisciplinary expertise, and a well-structured implementation strategy. These elements not only facilitate initial implementation but also ensure the system's adaptability to evolving sustainability objectives and technological advancements. The findings underscore the necessity of a structured approach to S-ERP implementation, emphasizing alignment with organizational sustainability goals and structural conditions to maximize benefits and mitigate risks. This study provides valuable insights for organizations aiming to integrate S-ERP systems effectively, highlighting both the opportunities and challenges in this evolving field.

articleTitle: A LLM-Based Platform for Flood Risk Education and Weather Alerts in SIDS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Small Island Developing States (SIDS) are particularly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, including hurricanes, flooding, and other extreme weather events. Effective flood risk education and near real-time weather alerts are critical for these regions. This paper presents a Proof of Concept (PoC) platform that leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) to process and deliver both static and real-time, country-specific information aimed at educating the public and generating targeted weather alerts. The LLM is augmented with climate, flooding, and weather data from various organizations and disaster management agencies, enabling it to provide context-specific, localized in-formation and educational resources. Unlike traditional methods, our approach integrates Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to enhance the accuracy and relevance of the generated outputs by referencing a fact-checked knowledge base before responding. Preliminary results demonstrate that the LLM, even at a smaller scale, delivers more accurate and context-specific information compared to standard models, underscoring the potential of LLM technology in addressing the unique challenges faced by SIDS. Future work will focus on scaling the model to improve performance and expanding its application to broader disaster management scenarios.

articleTitle: Unlocking Potential: Identifying and Overcoming Barriers to Innovation in the Energy Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: How do common barriers to innovation and the Valleys of Death (VoDs) challenge technological innovation within the energy sector, and which strategies are the most effective in overcoming these challenges? The focus of this article is to answer this question. This scoping review follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews review (PRISMA-ScR). Papers used in this review were identified through a search string developed and implemented in Scopus; keyword searches were conducted in Scopus, Google Scholar, and the Stellenbosch University Library; and relevant papers' reference lists were consulted. Three screening phases were implemented to narrow the papers, ensuring each corresponded to the inclusion criteria. Based on the literature, the four main categories of barriers to innovation were listed - social, financial, technological, and regulatory - along with several sub-barriers for each. Gaps in the literature were identified due to the lack of evidence in existing literature to answer the research questions developed for this review comprehensively. Further research will be conducted into trends within the barriers to innovation and methods to overcome the barriers experienced.

articleTitle: Construction Material Selection for Marine Water Quality: A Framework and Goal Programming Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: The paper proposes a framework and goal programming model for minimizing the environmental impact on marine water quality by optimizing building material selection. The model concentrates on five major construction categories: general construction, wall material, roof material, insulation material, and finishing. The goal of the model is to select the optimal combination of construction materials to reduce impact on coastal water quality. The steps of the framework consist of determining available material alternatives, selecting indicators of material impact on marine water quality, assigning weights to the indicators, and finally formulating the goal programming objective functions, constraints and targets. Six critical environmental indicators are were chosen based on literature investigation: eutrophication potential - marine (EP), acidification potential (AP), Comparative Toxic Unit for Humans (carcinogenic) (HTP-c), total global warming potential (GWP), water (user) deprivation potential (WDP), and potential comparative toxic unit for ecosystems (ETP). Environmental impact data for various building materials were gathered and weighted according to their significance to marine water quality. The goal programming model was formulated to minimize the environmental impacts on marine water quality. An example was then used for the application of the framework and model. For determining the ideal material combination for each category, an integer linear programming approach was used with MATLAB. The study emphasizes the importance of informed material selection in reducing environmental damage and establishes a solid foundation for future research and policy development in sustainable building design.

articleTitle: On the Detection of Manipulated Identification Documents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: As concerts and events have increased in scale, event organizers are forced to rely on ticket management systems to automate the admission to their events. As more event spaces can accommodate more patrons it has become more important to ensure that event spaces are not oversold. Many instances of duplicated and fake ticket admissions have led to catastrophe, violating regulations and creating unsafe situations for patrons. While online ticket sales increase customer convenience, they also increase accessibility for threat actors, which can potentially cause loss for the event organizers. One solution is to require a form of identification to gain admission to an event. However, currently, there exists a significant gap in reliably detecting manipulated identification documents, especially with the rapid improvements in artificial intelligence (AI). These advanced AI models can produce forged results that are so realistic that the artifacts and inconsistencies left behind are almost invisible to the average person. In this paper, we present a method for detecting documents that have been manipulated using face-swapping techniques by employing the power of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). This would aid in reducing the losses suffered by event organizers and prevent them from admitting fake or duplicated tickets while improving the convenience to legitimate customers.

articleTitle: Order Matching Mechanism in Order-Driven Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Order-driven financial markets are widely used for many asset classes. Trading mechanisms in order-driven market environments affect trader behavior. We investigate stability and liquidity in order-driven financial markets by using an agent-based model. We concentrate on continuous double auctions, the principle trading mechanism in this class, and consider a new order queuing mechanism: spread-price/time priority, an alternative recently defined in literature to reduce toxic order flows due to latency arms race. We find that as the market places more emphasis on spreads, it becomes more stable. Then we obtained a specific set of parameter settings through empirical game theory analysis that allow the spreadlprice-time priority order matching mechanism to ensure both low market volatility and substantial trading volume.

articleTitle: Mathematical Models Applications in Digital Supply Chain Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Nowadays supply chains are distinct than those of a few decades ago, and they're now evolving in a highly competitive environment. More clearly, supply chains can no longer be placed, only, in such a way that they can buy, make, move, or sell the right items in the adequate quantities in the right places rapidly. As a result, supply chains must become intelligent to successfully cope with the growing challenges. Many functional supply chain applications based on mathematical quantitave models have been used, however there have been few research on mathematical programming models applicability in the digital supply chain processes. For this reason, this paper aims to investigate the possible benefits of mathematical programming solutions in digital supply chains since we are aware of their potential benefits in the traditional one. We categorized the quantitative mathematical models used in digital supply chain management based on reviewing research articles published in this topic. Furthermore, we provided an integrated model illustrating the use of mathematical programming methods in the digital supply chain. The conceptualized framework aids in showing an overview of usable mathematical models in the digital supply chain. Because it outlines the important advantage and benefit of applying mathematical models integrated with novel technologies in the value chain.

articleTitle: A Review of Waste Management in the Healthcare Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Healthcare is a large sector that includes different facilities such as hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies. Such a large, complex sector generates huge amounts of solid waste which is typically considered hazardous, requiring special collection and disposal methods to ensure safe management. As such, the topic of healthcare waste management has been a subject of great interest to scholars and even more so since the covid-19 pandemic. This paper examines healthcare waste management, a complex field requiring in-depth research, by analyzing the literature acquired from the Scopus database using “healthcare waste management” and “medical waste management” as keywords, the paper identifies the nine key themes in literature and the emerging trends in the field. This review goes beyond existing summaries by highlighting well-researched areas such as healthcare waste management practices, as well as pinpointing gaps in knowledge such as the lack of frameworks to transition healthcare from a linear to a circular economy. This paper aims to offer a comprehensive overview of the current research, which informs future research directions and aids in developing improved healthcare waste management practices.

articleTitle: An AI Approach to SME Inventory Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: Inventory management has been widely studied for large companies in countries with land borders. We focus on the application of Data Science to Inventory Management of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Small Island Developing States (SIDs) which has the additional constraints that, the customer base is small and land-based delivery of products from other countries is not possible (i.e., only Sea and Air delivery is possible). In order to reduce costs, batch purchasing must be performed and this requires forecasting of products to be purchased as well as their quantities. We also need to take into account storage costs, shelf life of products and the reduction of the value of certain products (e.g., electronic items) over time. This requires a combination of accurate forecasting and opti-mized inventory management. We investigate both traditional and Machine Learning (ML) based approaches. Our results indicate that, although the ML models were generally good, the traditional models (such as seasonal naive and Holt-Winters) outperformed them in many cases due to the limited data available. We adopted a product-specific approach for the forecasting phase and then combined this with an optimized ordering strategy. With our approach, inventory was significantly reduced while maintaining the same level of customer satisfaction (i.e., availability of desired products).

articleTitle: Lean Construction in Action: Examining Practices in UAE Firms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: This study examines the lean practices (LPs) currently implemented by construction firms in the UAE, analyzing variations in their implementation frequency and identifying differences between small-medium firms (SMFs) and large construction firms. Data were collected from 257 construction firms through a structured questionnaire, revealing that 20 LPs are being applied across the industry, with a strong focus on minimizing waste, organizing procedures, and prioritizing accuracy and quality. The findings highlight significant disparities in adopting specific LPs between SMFs and large firms, particularly in areas such as continuous employee training, inventory management, technological advancements, and employee reward systems. These findings and their implications are expected to guide project managers in implementing LPs to enhance construction efficiency, reduce waste, and improve project delivery in UAE construction firms and other firms operating in similar environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Recommender Systems: A Practical Study on Loss Function Optimization in B2B Commerce
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Technology Management, Operations and Decisions (ICTMOD)
abstract: In this study, we present our work on developing a stock recommendation system for sales of industrial parts to customers at a mayor technical center in Jordan. The system leverages 40,000 transactions collected over a two-year period which are analyzed by machine learning to generate recommendations for internal decisions of whom to offer which product according to similarities between customers, items and past transactions. We compare collaborative filtering using matrix factorization with a hybrid model that exploits embedded item and user features such as categories and temporal buying behavior. Several loss functions are compared for both models, and we show that depending on the specific need of the user, either model shows better recommendation results. The study shows the importance of model selection and parameter fine-tuning when implementing a recommendation system in a B2B context, while also pointing out possible pitfalls in building such a system with real-world data.
